questions.question: Which of the following is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
Someone is sitting in the driver's seat of a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian that might move into your lane. If a driver beside you is too close to the car ahead, they may try to pass and cut in front of you. If you see someone in a parked car or a pedestrian in the street, honk as you pass. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together to see better.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may finish passing in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You may go over the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the speed limit when passing. You may only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
Stopping before you expect to.
A tire may burst.
Taking longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?

options.text: With the right hand
With the left hand
With the right foot
With the left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or put them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads high on the back of the seat or sissy bar because this raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Spread loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to look if you check your mirrors.
Your mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can trust that other drivers will see your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When turning a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Push the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Not grip the handlebars because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pushing the grip in the direction you want to turn will cause the correct lean.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Riding in heavy traffic.
Riding during the day in good conditions.
There are two lanes in each direction.
You think stopping will take a normal amount of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in heavy traffic.
questions.explanation: Give yourself more space in less-than-ideal conditions. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, you are riding at night, or traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: Increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
Riding conditions are normal.
The roadway is wet.
You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The roadway is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance if your motorcycle will need a longer distance to stop. Also increase your distance in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.
It is less effective than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face if you crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not protect your face like goggles or a face shield do.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your eyes and your face.
Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield can protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to avoid a crash?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Do not ride during the day.
Find safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To reduce your chance of a crash, be as visible as possible. Wear bright-colored clothing when you ride, even during the day.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To see if parked cars are moving into traffic.
To see if vehicles are changing lanes.
To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
To see if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
questions.explanation: When you stop at an intersection, use your mirrors to check for cars coming up from behind. The drivers may not see you, and you may need to move quickly.

questions.question: How should you secure a load in a sidecar?

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure it so the weight does not shift.
Place it loose in the seat.
Secure it near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it so the weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not move. Place heavy loads toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the nose from lifting up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on most motorcycles?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Before you ride, make sure you know where all your motorcycle's controls are.

questions.question: What should passengers do while riding?

options.text: Lean when the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding the operator and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When are motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When other drivers can see them.
When they are faster than other vehicles.
When they are on the side of the road.
When they are on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When other drivers can see them.
questions.explanation: Good riders know they are safest when other drivers see them clearly. Use your headlight, brake light, signals, and good lane position to be seen.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking next to a curb, park at a 90-degree angle with your rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you.
Is not worth the effort.
Does not mean they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield. Drivers often look at motorcycles but fail to notice them.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Keep a shorter distance behind other vehicles.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake later than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase your distance from other vehicles, and leave bigger gaps when merging.

questions.question: When riding at night, you can see better by:

options.text: Using the headlights of the car ahead of you.
Using your brake light.
Riding faster.
Getting closer to the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the headlights of the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: At night, use the headlights of the vehicle ahead to see the road better. Increase your following distance and slow down when riding in the dark.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and move to the side of the road.
Loosen your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and move to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep going straight. Brake only on the tire that is not flat. Slowly move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should ride in:

options.text: Single-file formation.
Staggered formation.
Pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of your lane.
Not worry about your position.
Always ride on the far right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. The driver ahead will most likely see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride in:

options.text: The left portion of your lane.
The right portion of your lane.
Any portion of your lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. Be ready to move as conditions change.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier because you can see the lights of other vehicles better.
Harder because it is more difficult to see.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than daytime riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder because it is more difficult to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is challenging because you cannot see as well, and other drivers cannot see you as easily. Low light makes it harder to judge distances.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel may be caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure.
Brakes not working properly.
Balanced cargo.
Strong wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with the right foot.
